intro.title: Discover the Old Bridge Heidelberg
intro.description: Welcome to Old Bridge Heidelberg – the historic Old Bridge (Alte Brücke) of Heidelberg, located in the heart of Heidelberg, Baden-Württemberg, Germany. As the city’s central hub for visitors, this famous stone bridge crosses the River Neckar and connects the Old Town with the Philosophers’ Walk. It is the ideal starting point for exploring Heidelberg Castle, the Old Town with Hauptstraße and the funicular to the Königstuhl. On the bridge you will find the Baroque bridge gate with its twin towers and the famous bronze bridge monkey – while the middle of the bridge offers one of the finest views over the river and the castle.

visitGuide.title: Visitor Tips
items: Free and accessible around the clock – open at any time for a stroll or photos
Best light early in the morning or late in the afternoon
It can be breezy on the bridge, so bring a light jacket
Many cafés and traditional German restaurants are located right in the Old Town

alsoKnownAs.title: Highlights
items: Historic architecture: An iconic stone bridge over the River Neckar with rich history and beautiful sculptures.
Perfect viewpoint: Offers a stunning panorama of Heidelberg Castle and the Old Town.
Central location: Steps away from Heidelberg's Old Town with many attractions within walking distance.

sections.title: History
sections.content: The Old Bridge (Karl Theodor Bridge) was built between 1786 and 1788 under Elector Karl Theodor and is the oldest surviving Neckar bridge in Heidelberg. The famous bridge monkey at the Old Town gate tower is one of its best-known symbols.

sections.title: Architecture
sections.content: The bridge is made of red sandstone and has nine arches. On the Old Town side stands the distinctive bridge gate with two round white towers, which served as a prison until 1822.

sections.title: Your Visit
sections.content: The Old Bridge is a public pedestrian and cycle crossing, free to use 24 hours a day. It connects the Old Town with the Philosophers' Walk and is the perfect starting point for a city tour.

hours.title: Opening Hours

hours.warningTime: Open to visitors around the clock
hours.tip: The Old Bridge is quietest in the early morning and late afternoon – perfect for a stroll or photos

transport.title: Getting There
transport.airportDesc: The nearest international airports are Frankfurt (FRA, about 80 km, ~1 hour by train or car) and Stuttgart (STR, about 120 km, ~1.5 hours by car).
transport.selfDriveDesc: From Frankfurt or Stuttgart you reach Heidelberg via the A5. The Old Town is car-free – use the parking garages P12 (Kornmarkt/castle) or P13 (Karlsplatz) and walk about 5–10 minutes to the Old Bridge.
transport.busDesc: ICE/IC trains run directly from Frankfurt and Stuttgart to Heidelberg's main station. Tram and bus lines take you into the Old Town within minutes.
transport.intercityDesc: The Old Town is compact: from the Old Bridge you can reach the castle funicular (Kornmarkt) and the Hauptstraße on foot within a few minutes.
transport.cyclingDesc: The Neckar riverside path and the Philosophers' Walk on the opposite bank are perfect for bike tours and hikes.
transport.tipsDesc: Heidelberg is located in Baden-Württemberg and makes an ideal base for exploring the Neckar region, Mannheim and Schwetzingen Palace.

route.title: Recommended Walking Route
route.overview: A Heidelberg Old Town stroll starting at the Old Bridge
steps: Start at the Old Bridge and visit the famous bridge monkey at the Old Town gate
Stroll along the River Neckar and enjoy the view of the Old Town and the castle
Walk through the bridge gate into the Old Town and explore the Hauptstraße pedestrian zone with its cafés and shops
Continue to the Marktplatz with the Church of the Holy Spirit – a great spot for coffee or lunch
Take the historic funicular from Kornmarkt up to Heidelberg Castle; if you have time, ride on to the Königstuhl
Cross the Old Bridge to the Philosophers' Walk on the opposite bank – the finest panorama of the city at sunset
supplements: The Old Bridge is a public foot and cycle path, free to use around the clock – no reservation needed.
There is little free parking in the Old Town – best to use one of the parking garages.
The path up to the castle leads over historic cobblestones – comfortable shoes are recommended.

items.name: Mark Weber
items.text: A beautifully preserved landmark! The stones and statues are full of history, and the view of the castle and the Neckar is priceless. Definitely come for sunset.

items.name: Julia Sanders
items.text: The most beautiful place in Heidelberg! From the bridge monkey to the panorama of the Old Town – simply stunning. It can get breezy, so bring a jacket in winter.

items.name: Tom Baker
items.text: An impressive structure. The bridge itself is not long, but the location is perfect – you can reach the Old Town or the castle within minutes. Parking can take a while in high season.

items.name: Anna Walker
items.text: So romantic! In the evening the illuminated bridge with the castle in the background is a dream. I completely fell in love with this city.

items.name: Peter Hoffman
items.text: The view instantly lifts your mood. From the bridge monkey to the river – everything is beautifully framed. Plenty of lovely cafés nearby.

items.name: Stephanie Brown
items.text: Absolutely worth seeing! From the Old Town you reach the bridge quickly. Comfortable shoes are a must – there is cobblestone everywhere. Tons of great photo spots!

items.name: Lucas Fisher
items.text: It feels like walking through history! Every arch and every statue has a story to tell. An absolute must on any visit to Heidelberg.

items.name: Christina Keller
items.text: More beautiful than any description. Whether the bridge monkey or the view upstream along the Neckar – you simply don't want to move on. The sunset from the middle of the bridge is unforgettable.

meta.description: The best attractions in Heidelberg at a glance: Heidelberg Castle, Königstuhl, Philosophers' Walk, Old Town & more – with distances from the Old Bridge and visitor tips.

attractions.title: Top Things to Do in Heidelberg Around the Old Bridge
intro: Heidelberg is one of Germany's most beautiful cities – and the Old Bridge sits right in the centre of its most famous sights. From here you can reach Heidelberg Castle, the Philosophers' Walk and the Old Town within a short walk.
This guide lists the most important attractions in Heidelberg with distances from the Old Bridge, notes on admission and opening hours, and practical tips for your visit.

items.name: Heidelberg Castle
items.distance: About 15 min uphill walk or 8 min by funicular
items.description: Heidelberg Castle is one of the world's most famous castle ruins and the city's landmark. From the castle garden and the terrace you get the iconic view down onto the Old Bridge and the Old Town. Inside, don't miss the Great Tun (the world's largest wine barrel), the German Pharmacy Museum and the lavish Renaissance apartments.

items.name: Königstuhl & Funicular Railway
items.distance: About 10 min more by funicular from the castle
items.description: At 568 m, the Königstuhl is the highest mountain in the region and offers some of the finest viewpoints over Heidelberg. The historic funicular has been running since 1890 in two sections from Kornmarkt via the castle up to the summit. At the top, a wide panorama over the Neckar valley, the Odenwald forest and the Rhine plain awaits – especially spectacular at sunset.

items.name: Philosophers' Walk
items.distance: About 20 min walk across the bridge
items.description: The Philosophers' Walk runs along the wooded slope on the opposite bank of the Neckar and is considered one of Germany's most beautiful promenades. It is named after the philosophers of Heidelberg University who once strolled here. It offers the most famous view of Heidelberg: the Old Town, the castle and the Old Bridge from the classic postcard angle.

items.name: Old Town & Hauptstraße
items.distance: Right at the Old Town end of the bridge
items.description: Heidelberg's Old Town with its Hauptstraße pedestrian zone is home to one of the longest shopping streets in Europe. Half-timbered houses, boutiques, cafés and beer gardens line the way from the Karlstor gate to University Square. In between you will find the Marktplatz with the Church of the Holy Spirit and plenty of traditional restaurants serving German cuisine.

items.name: Church of the Holy Spirit
items.distance: About 5 min walk from the bridge
items.description: The late-Gothic Church of the Holy Spirit on Marktplatz is the largest church in Heidelberg. It took over 150 years to build and once housed the famous Bibliotheca Palatina, whose books are now scattered around the world. A lively book market regularly takes place in front of the church.

items.name: Old University & Student Jail
items.description: Heidelberg University was founded in 1386 and is the oldest university in Germany. At University Square you can visit the Student Jail, a historic student prison from the 18th century whose walls are covered with graffiti left by former students. The Old Assembly Hall (Alte Aula) is also worth a look.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Your Visit
list: Early mornings are the quietest time at the castle and the Philosophers' Walk – ideal for photos without the crowds.
Castle and funicular are best combined in half a day; combination tickets save you queuing at the ticket office.
Most attractions are within walking distance. Comfortable shoes are recommended for the castle hill and the Philosophers' Walk.
Allow plenty of time: the viewpoints invite you to linger and the Old Town has plenty of culinary delights.

practicalInfo.title: Practical Tips for Your Visit
practicalInfo.subtitle: Toilets, parking, shopping, dining and more – compiled neutrally, without advertising for individual businesses.

groups.title: Public Toilets
items: Public facilities can be found in the Old Town and near the bridgehead; many cafés and restaurants also let guests use theirs.
Toilets are rare along the Philosophers' Path and in the castle grounds – plan ahead before your walk.

groups.title: Parking & Getting There
items: There is virtually no parking right at the bridge. Use the Old Town car parks or park-and-ride lots on the edge of town, 5–15 minutes' walk away.
Trams and buses run from the main station into the city centre; the bridge is a short walk from there.
Motorhomes and coaches have dedicated parking areas outside the Old Town.

groups.title: Food & Drink
items: Around the bridge you will find cafés, bakeries, ice-cream parlours and restaurants serving German and international cuisine.
For a picnic with a view of the bridge and castle, the Neckar meadows are ideal – self-catered and free of charge.

groups.title: Where to Stay
items: From Old Town hotels to guesthouses, holiday flats and hostels – there is something for every budget.
Accommodation on the north bank of the Neckar is often quieter and faces the Old Town and castle.

groups.title: Shopping & Everyday Needs
items: Supermarkets, drugstores, souvenir shops, pharmacies and ATMs line the pedestrian zone on Hauptstraße.
Good to know: in Germany most shops close on Sundays – plan your errands for weekdays.

groups.title: Fuel & Charging
items: Petrol stations are located on the main roads out of town and at the edge of the city – not in the pedestrian zone.
Charging points for electric cars and e-bikes are available at car parks and public parking spaces across the city.

history.title: History, Architecture & Legends
history.subtitle: From the first wooden bridge through war and rebuilding to today's bronze bridge monkey: the eventful story of a landmark.

timeline.title: The first documented bridge
timeline.text: A Neckar bridge at this spot is first documented in 1284. Wooden bridges of the time had a hard life: as early as 1288 an ice drift destroyed the structure – a fate shared by many of its successors.

timeline.title: The War of the Palatine Succession
timeline.text: In March 1689 French troops under General Mélac blew up the then bridge; in 1693 they ravaged the city once more. For about two decades ferries and a pontoon bridge crossed the Neckar until a new bridge was built in 1706–1708.

timeline.title: The Karl Theodor Bridge rises
timeline.text: Elector Karl Theodor commissioned building inspector Mathias Mayer to construct today's bridge. In just two years a roughly 200-metre stone bridge with nine barrel vaults was built, clad in red sandstone – and it still bears the name of its patron.

timeline.title: The Bridge Gate with its twin towers
timeline.text: The nearly 28-metre twin towers of the bridge gate rise at the southern end. Their core dates from the late-Gothic town wall of the 15th century; the gate was remodelled in the Baroque style in 1709/11. Here the city collected the bridge toll – and in times of danger a portcullis sealed off the entrance.

timeline.title: Destruction in the Second World War
timeline.text: Shortly before American troops entered Heidelberg, Wehrmacht engineers blew up the Neckar bridges. Three arches of the Old Bridge collapsed into the river. Reconstruction began on 14 March 1946 – the rebuilt bridge was ceremonially reopened on 26 July 1947.

timeline.title: The return of the bridge monkey
timeline.text: As early as the 17th century a stone monkey holding a mirror sat on the bridge – a mocking reminder that anyone gazing in wonder at the town is just another "old monkey". The monkey, destroyed in 1689, was recreated in 1979 as a bronze sculpture by Gernot Rumpf; its hollow head still invites visitors to pose for photos.

history.quote: "Why do you gape at me? Haven't you seen the old monkey of Heidelberg?" – a mocking rhyme that has accompanied the bridge monkey since the 17th century.
facts: 200 metres long, 7 metres wide and up to 10.4 metres above the Neckar.
Nine barrel vaults span the river; individual spans range from 12.2 to 22 metres.
The 2nd and 7th of 8 pillars are wider – they were once intended to carry statues.
The exterior is faced in red sandstone, the interior is rubble masonry.
Only the two land arches were rebuilt in 1969/70 – the historic appearance of the bridge is unchanged.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions – Old Bridge Heidelberg
faq.subtitle: Short, factual answers – from the exact location and admission to tips for combining your visit.

items.q: Where exactly is the Old Bridge Heidelberg located?
items.a: Old Bridge Heidelberg crosses the River Neckar at the edge of Heidelberg’s Old Town in Baden-Württemberg, Germany. The bridge gate with its twin towers sits at the southern end next to the Old Town; on the opposite bank a path leads up to the Philosophers’ Walk. Address for navigation: Alte Brücke, 69117 Heidelberg, Germany.

items.q: Is it free to visit the Old Bridge?
items.a: Yes. The Old Bridge is a public pedestrian and cycle bridge and can be crossed free of charge at any time – there is no admission, no gate and no seasonal closure.

items.q: When was the Old Bridge built?
items.a: The present stone bridge was built in 1786–1788 under Elector Karl Theodor and is therefore also called the Karl-Theodor-Brücke. It replaced earlier wooden bridges on this site that are documented as early as 1284.

items.q: Can you drive across the Old Bridge?
items.a: No. The bridge is open to pedestrians and cyclists only. Motorised traffic uses the neighbouring road bridges across the Neckar.

items.q: What is the bridge monkey and where is it?
items.a: The bronze bridge monkey sits at the bridge gate on the Old Town side. The 1979 figure recalls a stone monkey from the 17th century that mocked curious onlookers; visitors still put their head into its hollow head for the traditional photo.

items.q: Which view from the Old Bridge is the most famous?
items.a: From the middle of the bridge you have the classic view of Heidelberg Castle and the Old Town. From the Philosophers’ Walk on the opposite bank you get the famous postcard panorama of the bridge, the Old Town and the castle.

items.q: What can I combine with a visit to the Old Bridge?
items.a: The bridge is the ideal starting point: Heidelberg Castle with the funicular (about 8–15 minutes), the Old Town with Hauptstraße and the Church of the Holy Spirit (5–10 minutes) and the Philosophers’ Walk on the other bank are all easy to reach on foot.
